caveats: Identity boundary: Jin Sung-Il is the North Korean national charged under that name in S.D. Fla. No. 1:25-cr-20021-DPG. Jin Song-Il is a reported alternate spelling; Pedro Alonso, Richard Stewart, Stewart Conn, and Kelsey Bane are indictment-attributed personas, not verified civil identities. The FBI separately publishes Pedro Alonso de los Reyes as an alias string, while the indictment names Pedro Ernesto Alonso de los Reyes as a separate co-defendant; that source conflict does not authorize a merge. Do not merge identity-theft victims, accounts, or images with this subject.
Charges are allegations; the subject is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.
Do not infer biometric identity, match the image to another persona, or identify a stolen-identity victim.
FBI pages may change; retain verification date.
Prefer link-only until rights and insignia review is complete.
The direct asset is reference metadata only and is not approved for caching.
The FBI image may be historical and may not reflect the subject's current appearance.
The official photograph is a legal-name wanted image; it must not be used as a portrait of an identity-theft victim whose name or document was used in the scheme.
Wanted and charged status does not establish guilt.
Persona names shown here are labels reported by the cited publisher. They are not asserted to be anyone's legal name, and unrelated real people who share a name are not implicated.

'Pedro Alonso' is the real name of co-defendant Pedro Ernesto Alonso De Los Reyes, whose identity the indictment alleges Jin used, with Alonso's consent, to obtain employment (overt acts 1-2, PDF pp. 13-14). It is a real person's name and is not shown as a persona.

'Kelsey Bane' is the name on an allegedly fraudulent U.S. passport described in the indictment; the indictment does not state whose personal information it carried. Do not assume a real Kelsey Bane is involved.
'Richard Stewart' and 'Stewart Conn' appear only as a/k/a entries in the indictment caption; no specific allegation describes their use.
Accounts and handles are historical observations reported by the cited sources. Present control of any account is not asserted, and a persona name is not asserted to be anyone's legal identity.
